name: Golden Horse Seafood Restaurant
why: One of two Chinese kitchens left in the historic Chinatown blocks, and the last spot nearby still serving a Cantonese lunch.
open_evidence: Hoodline report on the last two Chinatown eateries, Feb 2026; Travel Portland Old Town guide, 2026

name: Mandarin House
why: One of the few Chinese kitchens still hanging on in greater Old Town, a plain room off Ankeny that the food press rarely mentions.
open_evidence: Named as still open in Old Town in Hoodline's Chinatown report, Feb 2026

name: Yokai Musubi
why: A tiny takeout room for onigiri and Spam musubi; a teriyaki salmon rice ball still costs under five dollars.
open_evidence: Willamette Week Cheap Eats, June 2026, with hours of 9 am to 4 pm Tuesday to Saturday

name: Kingston Bar & Grill
why: A longtime tavern on the doorstep of Providence Park where fans eat before matches; plain bar food, done without pretense.
open_evidence: Participant in the Portland Mercury's Burger Week, Aug 2026

name: Nong's Khao Man Gai
why: Nong Poonsukwattana built a cult on one plate: poached chicken, garlicky rice and her ginger-soybean sauce, born in a cart.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly's 25 Restaurants That Made Portland, Nov 2025; Travel Portland Central Eastside guide

name: LaurelThirst Public House
why: A worn-in Kerns tavern with a kitchen and free folk and bluegrass sets nearly every night, some running past ten.
open_evidence: EverOut calendar lists shows through Oct 2026, including a Sunday 9 to 11:30 pm open mic

name: Tabor Bread
why: Mills its own whole grains for dark, wood-fired loaves at the quiet top of Hawthorne; toast and a coffee make the morning.
open_evidence: Finalist, Best Bakery, Willamette Week readers' poll, July 2026

name: Taquería Los Puñales
why: Small Belmont taqueria cooking Mexico City style; the chilaquiles have a following, and readers ranked it second-best Mexican in 2026.
open_evidence: Second place, Best Mexican Restaurant, Willamette Week readers' poll, July 2026; Travel Portland Belmont guide

name: Ricky's
why: Spielman's Division bagel shop, renamed this month by the family for the late father who opened the first Spielman on this street. Same boiled bagels.
open_evidence: Bridgetown Bites, Oct 2026: shop renamed Ricky's on Oct 26, 2026, menu largely unchanged

name: Dot's Cafe
why: Clinton Street bar and diner that has fed night owls for decades: dim booths, kitsch on the walls, burgers and fries well past ten.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly Division/Clinton guide, about Feb 2026, and bar-crawl guide, about Mar 2026

name: Bertie Lou's Cafe
why: A twenty-odd-seat Sellwood breakfast room known for cinnamon roll French toast and oversized breakfast burritos. Get there early on weekends or wait outside.
open_evidence: Perfect score in Portland Tribune inspection roundup, Apr 2026; Portland Monthly brunch guide, Nov 2025

name: Brooklyn Park Pub
why: Low-key Brooklyn corner pub with a whiskey club, regulars at the rail and baskets of tots. The neighborhood mostly keeps it to itself.
open_evidence: Perfect score in Portland Tribune inspection roundup, Jun 2026

name: Taqueria La Hidalguense
why: Small outer-Foster taqueria named for Hidalgo, the Mexican state famous for lamb barbacoa. Almost unwritten about, so ask about the weekend special.
open_evidence: Listed in Portland Tribune county inspection roundup, Feb 2026

name: Red's Bar and Grill
why: Foster-Powell regulars' bar with pub grub and Bloody Marys. No scene, just a burger, a stool and the same faces every week.
open_evidence: Perfect score in Portland Tribune inspection roundup, Jul 2026

name: Kenny's Noodle House
why: Powell Boulevard noodle shop with dozens of congee and noodle soup combinations. A regulars' room a few blocks off the 82nd crowds.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly Chinese food guide, updated about Dec 2025

name: Excellent Cuisine
why: Dim sum by day and a Cantonese dinner menu at night, in the former Wong's King space on SE Division.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly 50 Best Restaurants list, Oct 2026

name: Roman Russian Market
why: A Russian grocery open two decades, with a deli counter turning out plov and shashlik and a pastry case piled with crepes and slab cakes.
open_evidence: Travel Oregon Slavic food guide, Apr 2026, describes the in-store cafe as open daily; also OPB gallery and Portland Monthly listing

name: J Vein Caffè
why: One owner, JJ Johnson, pulling Italian-style cappuccinos and affogatos from a converted Airstream in the Rose City Food Park pod since 2019.
open_evidence: Portland Mercury Top 20 Food Carts, Food Issue Jul 2026; Portland Monthly indie coffee guide notes owner-run since 2019

name: Bollywood Theater
why: Counter-service Indian street food on Alberta, with thalis and snacks served in a room hung with Bollywood posters; a readers' favorite in 2026.
open_evidence: Second place, Best Indian, Willamette Week Best of Portland readers' poll, Jul 2026 (brand has two shops)

name: Hat Yai
why: Fried chicken in the style of Hat Yai in southern Thailand, with flaky roti and a cup of curry for dipping.
open_evidence: Second place, Best Thai, Willamette Week Best of Portland readers' poll, Jul 2026 (brand has two shops)

name: ¿Por Qué No?
why: Portland readers' top Mexican pick in 2026, a bright, packed Mississippi taqueria with a line out the door; get the carnitas taco.
open_evidence: Winner, Best Mexican, Willamette Week Best of Portland readers' poll, Jul 2026 (brand has two shops)

name: Queen of Sheba
address: 2413 NE Martin Luther King Jr Blvd
why: Readers picked it as Portland's best Ethiopian in 2026: platters of wots and tibs on injera in a dining room on MLK in Eliot.
open_evidence: Winner, Best Ethiopian, Willamette Week Best of Portland readers' poll, Jul 2026

name: Mi Burrito
why: Lombard Street burrito shop near Interstate with more than 30 burrito options, still priced at ten dollars or less when that has become rare.
open_evidence: Listed in Willamette Week's ten-dollar burrito roundup, Mar 2026

name: Thai Cottage
why: Plain Lombard Street Thai room a few doors from Tienda Santa Cruz, named by a St. Johns chef as one of her regular dinner stops.
open_evidence: Recommended in Willamette Week, May 2026; OpenStreetMap survey Jul 2026

name: Lily Market
why: Halsey Street Asian grocery near Gateway whose deli counter packs salad rolls, steamed buns, egg rolls and teriyaki chicken to eat on the go.
open_evidence: OpenStreetMap survey of the market and its deli with current hours, Jul and Aug 2026

name: Rose City Burrito
why: Cully burrito shop on Prescott that Willamette Week named in 2026 as one of the few places still filling a burrito for ten dollars.
open_evidence: Listed in Willamette Week's ten-dollar burrito roundup, Mar 2026

name: Barbur World Foods
why: Barbur Boulevard grocery with a Middle Eastern deli case and a wood-fired oven baking pita to order; assemble a takeout spread of hummus and salads.
open_evidence: Featured in Willamette Week's Westside specialty markets guide, May 2026

name: Banning's Restaurant & Pie House
why: Pacific Highway diner and pie house since 1979, once one of the area's rare all-night stops; order a slice of the scratch-made pie.
open_evidence: Listed with a score of 100 in a Valley Times east Washington County inspection roundup (late-July inspections), Aug 2026

name: Coredam
why: Canyon Road Korean room known for yangnyeom gejang, raw crab in a spicy chile marinade, the dish Korean regulars seek out.
open_evidence: Listed in Portland Monthly Beaverton guide dated Apr 2026; hours not confirmed

name: Sanguiche
why: The Spillette family's small downtown shop for Italian sandwiches; on Wednesdays the cannoli are filled fresh until they run out.
open_evidence: Gresham Outlook feature Mar 2026 with hours (9:30 am to 6 pm, Wed to Sun)

name: Las Brasas
why: Mom-and-pop Costa Rican rotisserie at Division and Main, opened February 2026; the spit-roasted chicken is the order.
open_evidence: Gresham Outlook feature Feb 2026; county inspection at this address reported Sep 2026

name: Murata
why: A long-running downtown Japanese room with no fusion and no fuss; go at lunch for bento and teriyaki among office regulars.
open_evidence: Listed in Travel Portland's downtown dining guide, page revised in 2026 (notes a Jan 2026 closure elsewhere)

name: Republic Cafe and Ming Lounge
why: Portland's oldest Chinese restaurant, open since 1922 under the Mui family; dinner only now, and far quieter than its history deserves.
open_evidence: Hoodline, Feb 2026: still operating, no longer open for lunch

name: The Sultan Cafe
why: Owner-run Slabtown grill that neighbors treat as their own kitchen; hummus with warm pita and shawarma are the order.
open_evidence: Owner Maher Makboul quoted as running the cafe in Willamette Week, June 2026; Axios underrated list, May 2024

name: Goose Hollow Inn
why: Opened in 1967 by the late mayor Bud Clark, still family run; the Reuben goes through a pizza oven for crackly rye.
open_evidence: Recommended in a March 2026 travel guide; EverOut keeps a current listing

name: Devil's Dill
why: Buckman sandwich shop that keeps slicing after most kitchens close; readers ranked it second for late-night eats in 2026.
open_evidence: Second place, Best Late-Night Eats, Willamette Week readers' poll, July 2026

name: Cricket Cafe
why: Unfussy Belmont breakfast room with a long vegan and gluten-free list, so a table with mixed diets can all order well.
open_evidence: Featured in Travel Portland's Belmont guide, revised in 2026

name: Space Room Lounge
why: Dark, loud, retro-futurist dive at the top of Hawthorne with stiff cheap pours and a grill working into the night.
open_evidence: Included in Portland Monthly's dive bar guide, Nov 2025

name: Lauretta Jean's
why: Pie by the slice from a baker who began at farmers markets: flaky butter crust, seasonal fruit fillings, and coffee in a calm Division room.
open_evidence: Portland Tribune county inspection roundup, Mar 2026; Portland Monthly Division/Clinton guide, about Feb 2026

name: Scottie's Pizza Parlor
why: Slice shop on Division where the dough ferments slowly and the pepperoni curls into cups. Order by the slice at the counter, no ceremony.
open_evidence: Named in Portland Monthly Division/Clinton neighborhood guide, about Feb 2026

name: Sebastiano's
why: Sicilian deli that left Montavilla for SE 13th, still known for cannoli and a Northwest take on the muffuletta piled with house-cured meats.
open_evidence: Perfect score at the Sellwood address, Portland Tribune inspection roundup, Jun 2026

name: Kay's Bar
why: Corner tavern at Milwaukie and Bybee since 1934. Weekday happy hour fills the booths with cheap nachos and heaping platters of fries.
open_evidence: Listed in Portland Tribune county inspection roundup, Feb 2026

name: Bar Carlo
why: Foster Road breakfast cafe that has anchored weekend mornings on the strip for years. Hearty egg plates, strong coffee and a neighborhood crowd.
open_evidence: Perfect score in Portland Tribune inspection roundup, Mar 2026

name: Pho Saigon Xua
why: Pho shop on the Foster-Powell side of 82nd with no press trail at all. The name nods to old Saigon; start with the beef pho.
open_evidence: Perfect score in Portland Tribune inspection roundup, Mar 2026

name: HK Cafe
why: Big strip-mall dim sum hall on 82nd with push carts. Weekend mornings bring a crowd and a long parade of har gow and chicken feet.
open_evidence: Named in Portland Tribune county inspection roundup headline, Oct 2026

name: Roscoe's
why: Montavilla beer bar that shares a kitchen and a back passage with Miyamoto, so fresh sushi lands beside your pint. A dive with a secret.
open_evidence: Willamette Week dive-bar sushi feature, Jul 2026; Montavilla News history piece, Apr 2026

name: Kee's #Loaded Kitchen
address: 3625 NE Martin Luther King Jr Blvd
why: Kee Nelson, who grew up in Northeast Portland, serves cornmeal catfish, wings and pork chops from a lot on MLK; get the mac and Kees.
open_evidence: Portland Mercury Top 20 Food Carts, Jul 2026, at 3625 NE MLK; Portland Monthly profile placed it in an MLK parking lot, Aug 2023

name: Abyssinian Kitchen
why: Ethiopian and Eritrean cooking that closed in the pandemic and came back on Alberta in 2022; the Oregonian ranked it among Portland's best.
open_evidence: Finalist, Best Ethiopian, Willamette Week Best of Portland readers' poll, Jul 2026

name: Tienda Santa Cruz
why: Taqueria tucked behind the aisles of a Mexican grocery and panaderia; huge, cheap tacos and burritos, plus pan dulce from the bakery case for later.
open_evidence: Recommended in Willamette Week, May 2026; in Travel Portland cheap eats guide updated Sept 2026; OpenStreetMap survey with hours Jul 2026

name: Kabuki Sushi & Grill
why: Small sushi-and-grill spot on the St. Johns main drag that a neighborhood chef lists among her everyday picks; a quiet alternative to Lombard's bars.
open_evidence: Recommended in Willamette Week, May 2026; OpenStreetMap survey Jul 2026

name: Pip's Original Doughnuts & Chai
why: Tiny Fremont Street shop frying small doughnuts to order alongside house-made chai; Portland readers voted it the city's best doughnut in 2026.
open_evidence: Won Best Doughnut in Willamette Week's readers' poll, Jul 2026; OpenStreetMap survey with hours Aug 2026

name: El Sombrero Tapatio
why: Parkrose fixture since 2002; Mama Elvira, who came from Jalisco in the 1970s, anchors a kitchen run by relatives and old family friends.
open_evidence: Hollywood Star News profile reprinted by Bridgetown Bites, Jun 2026

name: South Store Cafe
why: Farm-country cafe far out on Scholls Ferry Road, a breakfast-sandwich and pastry stop that a 2025 regional brunch roundup ranked ninth.
open_evidence: Listed in a Hillsboro News-Times inspection roundup of late-June inspections, Jul 2026

name: My Place Tavern
why: Forest Grove neighborhood tavern on 21st Avenue with a working kitchen and a perfect 2026 inspection; no food press at all, just locals.
open_evidence: Scored 100 in a Forest Grove News-Times inspection roundup of late-May inspections, Jun 2026

name: McCrae's Country Cafe
why: Unfussy country cafe on West Powell, an East County breakfast stop with almost no press, worth a reviewer's visit to name its best plate.
open_evidence: County health inspection Feb 2026, reported by the Gresham Outlook Mar 2026; hours not confirmed

name: Milwaukie Pizza Co.
why: Family-run pizza shop in a McLoughlin strip mall since 2021; slices and big pies from a stone-deck oven with a honey-kissed crust.
open_evidence: That Oregon Life feature Sep 2026; hours not confirmed

name: Fuller's Coffee Shop
why: Looping Formica counters and swivel stools since 1947; breakfast runs all day and the cheeseburger recipe has never changed.
open_evidence: Own site posts a Feb 2026 announcement; Silicon Florist visitor guide recommends it July 2026

name: Xin Ding Dumpling House
why: Handmade pork and shrimp xiao long bao in an Old Town room with space for a whole family table, rare downtown.
open_evidence: Named as still open in Old Town in Hoodline's Chinatown report, Feb 2026

name: Stepping Stone Cafe
why: Began as a 1948 soda fountain; the plate-sized Mancakes are the move, and the sass on the menu comes free.
open_evidence: Featured in Travel Portland's Slabtown and Nob Hill guides, revised in 2026

name: Escape From New York Pizza
why: Nob Hill slice counter since 1983, thin and foldable, served with a gruff attitude that regulars would miss.
open_evidence: Featured in Travel Portland's Nob Hill guide, revised in 2026

name: The Paper Bridge
why: Its co-owners cook Hanoi food in the old La Luna space; bun cha and Haiphong crab spring rolls are the reason to go.
open_evidence: Axios Portland feature, Feb 2026

name: The Waffle Window
why: You order through a side window and eat on the sidewalk; the savory bacon, cheddar and jalapeño waffle beats the sweet ones.
open_evidence: Featured in Travel Portland's Hawthorne guide, revised in 2026

name: Horse Brass Pub
why: Fifty years of cask ale, Scotch eggs, sausage rolls and fish and chips, plus dawn crowds for English football.
open_evidence: KOIN on its 50th anniversary party, July 2026; Willamette Week World Cup story, June 2026

name: Pinolo Gelato
why: Small-batch gelato from an Italian-born owner, kept in lidded steel wells the old way. Order the pine nut flavor the shop is named for.
open_evidence: Named in Portland Monthly Division/Clinton neighborhood guide, about Feb 2026

name: Nuestra Cocina
why: Family-run Division dining room cooking regional Mexican plates and moles since the early 2000s, long before the street filled with condos and lines.
open_evidence: Perfect score in Portland Tribune county inspection roundup, Mar 2026

name: Original Hotcake House
why: Longtime Powell Boulevard diner with plate-sized hotcakes, a jukebox and gruff charm. No longer open all night, but still flipping until 11 pm.
open_evidence: Diner reviews dated Dec 2025 on a listings page; Wikipedia snapshot of Mar 2026 describes it as operating. Weakest evidence in this set

name: Off the Griddle
why: A fully vegan diner run like an old neighborhood breakfast joint, with biscuits and gravy, scrambles and griddle plates. Nobody misses the bacon.
open_evidence: Listed in Portland Monthly brunch guide dated Nov 2025

name: Woodstock Wine & Deli
why: Family-run Woodstock wine shop and deli since 1985, whose owner credits his parents. Sandwiches, newer barbecue, and a bottle pulled off the shelf.
open_evidence: Listed as Woodstock Wine Deli & BBQ in Portland Tribune county inspection roundup, Mar 2026

name: Master Kong
why: Sibling-run cafe since 2018 mixing northern Tianjin and Cantonese home cooking: congee, wonton noodle soup and fried dough sticks for breakfast.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly Chinese food guide, updated about Dec 2025

name: Mis Tacones
why: A Mexican kitchen on Killingsworth that started as a pop-up and made a New York Times list of the country's best Mexican restaurants.
open_evidence: Finalist, Best Mexican, Willamette Week Best of Portland readers' poll, Jul 2026

name: John Street Cafe
why: Breakfast-and-brunch St. Johns standby with a sunny patio and a whiteboard of specials; order the giant filbert-and-currant pancakes.
open_evidence: OpenStreetMap entry re-surveyed with current hours Jun 2026; Portland Monthly listing (undated)

name: Mikasa Sushi & Ramen
why: Sushi and ramen house at the far end of the St. Johns strip, open lunch through dinner, that a local chef names among her regulars.
open_evidence: Recommended in Willamette Week, May 2026; OpenStreetMap survey with hours Jul 2026

name: Panaderia y Pasteleria La Imperial
why: TV Highway panaderia and pasteleria baking pan dulce, desserts and wedding cakes; Hillsboro picked it for a 2026 small-business stabilization grant.
open_evidence: On the City of Hillsboro 2026 Small Business Stabilization award list (published about Apr 2026); directory lists 8am to 9pm hours

name: El Rinconcito Mexicano
why: Mexican kitchen in the same TV Highway strip as La Imperial panaderia, so dinner and pan dulce are one stop; unreviewed by the food press.
open_evidence: Listed (score 77) in a Forest Grove News-Times inspection roundup, Jun 2026

name: OG Birrieria
why: Started as a Hillsboro taco truck; its Lake Grove storefront, open since April 2026, centers on birria tacos with consome for dipping.
open_evidence: Lake Oswego Review on its soft opening, Apr 2026; hours not confirmed

name: B&b Pizza Co.
why: Troutdale pizza parlor built to feel like a 1980s family pizzeria, with a thin house sourdough crust and cornmeal; Outlook readers' best pizza for 2026.
open_evidence: The Outlook 2026 Readers Choice best pizza feature, Mar 2026

name: Kelly's Olympian
why: Downtown bar from 1902 with old motorcycles overhead, a working kitchen, and shows or open mics most nights.
open_evidence: EverOut lists its Dark Arts Fest running through Oct 31, 2026 and a Burger Week burger, Aug 2026

name: Ken's Artisan Bakery
why: The 2001 bakery that taught Portland slow-fermented bread, now owned by longtime staff; come early for a croissant and a country loaf.
open_evidence: Featured in Travel Portland's Nob Hill guide, revised in 2026

name: Nicholas Restaurant
why: The Dibe family's Lebanese room since 1987; the mezze platter and pita puffed hot from the oven keep its small dining room full.
open_evidence: Travel Portland Middle Eastern food guide, updated June 2026

name: Jam on Hawthorne
why: A Hawthorne breakfast standby that placed second in the 2026 readers' brunch vote; go on a weekday to skip the weekend line.
open_evidence: Second place, Best Brunch Spot, Willamette Week readers' poll, July 2026

name: DC Vegetarian
why: A onetime downtown food cart now holding a Division storefront, stacking seitan cheesesteaks and hearty vegan sandwiches that win over meat eaters. Cheap and filling.
open_evidence: Perfect score in Portland Tribune county inspection roundup, Mar 2026

name: Reel M Inn
why: Tiny fishing-themed dive where fried chicken and jojos are cooked to order, so you nurse a beer and wait. The wait is the point.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly bar-crawl guide, updated about Mar 2026

name: Rose VL Deli
why: Sister shop to Ha VL, running a short daily soup rotation until each pot sells out. The Saturday turmeric noodle soup is the one.
open_evidence: Listed in Portland Monthly brunch guide dated Nov 2025

name: Lutz Tavern
why: Woodstock tavern open since 1947, with old booths, cheap pints and pub food. Willamette Week tied it to the early-2000s Pabst revival.
open_evidence: Bridgetown Bites Dry January 2026 roundup, published Dec 2025

name: Fortune BBQ Noodle House
why: Corner Cantonese barbecue shop at Burnside and 82nd, in a former gyro stand. Roast duck and char siu over rice or noodle soup, cheaply.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly Chinese food guide, updated about Dec 2025

name: Slim's Restaurant & Lounge
why: Lombard Street dive pouring for more than a century, with live music, cheap happy-hour beer and real bar food; get the jalapeno poppers.
open_evidence: Named a regular haunt by a St. Johns chef in Willamette Week, May 2026; OpenStreetMap survey Jul 2026

name: Reedville Cafe
why: Roadside cafe feeding Reedville from TV Highway for about 75 years; new owners since 2025, and readers ranked it Hillsboro's second-best restaurant in 2024.
open_evidence: Named in a Hillsboro News-Times health inspection roundup headline, Jul 2026; new-ownership story May 2025

name: Nak Won
why: Old guard of Beaverton's Korean row since 2001; order the peppery, barely sauced tteokbokki or the black-bean jajangmyun.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly Beaverton guide dated Apr 2026; Downtown Beaverton Association business listing with current hours

name: Taqueria Rico Taco
why: Handmade tacos on SE 181st since 1999; this Rockwood standby gave free meals to SNAP families during the 2025 shutdown.
open_evidence: Gresham Outlook feature Nov 2025; hours not confirmed

name: Birrias Tamazula
why: No-frills room just off downtown Gresham's main drag, open since 2022, whose birria Portland Monthly ranked among the metro's best bowls; get the consome.
open_evidence: Weak: a map listing shows customer reviews into early 2026; no press since the Nov 2023 review

name: Luc Lac Vietnamese Kitchen
why: Feeds downtown long after the shows let out; order the shaking beef the place is named for.
open_evidence: Won Best Late-Night Eats and Best Vietnamese in Willamette Week's readers' poll, July 2026

name: Broder Cafe
why: Small Clinton Street room since 2007 cooking Scandinavian breakfasts: baked eggs in skillets over hash, Swedish meatballs, and aebleskiver with lingonberry. Arrive early.
open_evidence: Listed in Portland Monthly brunch guide dated Nov 2025

name: Otto's Sausage Kitchen
why: Family meat market on Woodstock for about a century, making over 40 sausages in house. Get the old-fashioned wiener and work the mustard bar.
open_evidence: Second place, Best Deli, Willamette Week Best of Portland readers' poll, Jul 2026

name: Bipartisan Cafe
why: Montavilla's long-running coffee and pie house, credited with kick-starting the Stark Street revival. Take a slice to a table under the political portraits.
open_evidence: Montavilla News, Sep 2026: jazz festival discount partner

name: Tom's Pancake House
why: Canyon Road pancake house serving Beaverton since 1966, often called the city's longest-running restaurant; a short stack here is suburban history.
open_evidence: Named in a Beaverton Valley Times health inspection roundup headline, Jul 2026; 1966 start per Washington County visitors bureau listing

name: Helvetia Tavern
why: Farm-country roadhouse under a ceiling of trucker hats; go for a big burger and fries after a drive past the fields.
open_evidence: That Oregon Life mom-and-pop list, Apr 2026

name: Polar King
why: Burger stand opened in 1952 when drive-ins lined Powell Boulevard, and it outlasted most of them; ten burgers on the board, chili cheeseburger first.
open_evidence: Polar King Restaurant scored 100 in The Outlook's Multnomah County inspection roundup, Sep 2026; KOIN history piece 2024

name: Gubanc's
why: The Gubanc family's Lake Grove pub since 1976, back in a remodeled room for its 50th year of feeding the neighborhood.
open_evidence: Own site announces reopening in remodeled space and its 50th year (est. 1976, so 2026)

name: Huber's Cafe
why: Oregon's oldest restaurant: roast turkey plates and Spanish coffee set alight at the table, now run by the Louie family's next generation.
open_evidence: Featured in Travel Portland's downtown guide, revised 2026; OPB on the family handover, July 2025

name: Ha VL
why: Family soup shop where each noodle soup appears on one day of the week. Check the schedule, come early, and expect it to sell out.
open_evidence: Portland Monthly 50 Best Restaurants list, Oct 2026

name: Oyatsupan Bakers
why: Japanese bakery in a Five Oaks strip since 2016, now with a Tigard shop; melonpan in a run of flavors and soft shokupan draw people.
open_evidence: Wikipedia records a new SE Portland kitchen opened in 2026; listings post Mon to Sat 8am to 6pm hours (no 2026 press found)

name: Babica Hen Cafe
why: Lake Grove breakfast cafe run by Joe Buck, grandson of Gubanc's founder; specialty waffles, benedicts and sticky buns, Bloody Marys for slow mornings.
open_evidence: Lake Oswego Review, Aug 2026, names Joe Buck as its current owner-operator; directory lists 8am to 2pm hours

name: Pine Shed Ribs
why: Pilkington Road barbecue joint smoking ribs until they sell out, with a pastry-and-pint sister, Piglet, two doors down for mornings.
open_evidence: Own site posts Mon to Sat 11am to 8pm hours; customer reviews dated Jan 2026 on a map listing
